headline_marked: [[Spot Robot]] Gets Korean Voice Control via VIDRAFT On-Device AI
headline: Spot Robot Gets Korean Voice Control via VIDRAFT On-Device AI
summary: VIDRAFT enables Korean voice commands for Boston Dynamics' Spot robot at Seoul RAIM, keeping all data processing local and off the cloud.
details: VIDRAFT has successfully integrated Korean-language voice control for Boston Dynamics' Spot robot at the Seoul Robot & AI Museum. This groundbreaking deployment allows the robot to understand and respond to Korean commands without any modifications to its existing hardware or manufacturer firmware.

The system operates entirely on-device, meaning all voice data is processed locally. This design choice ensures privacy by keeping sensitive audio information off the cloud and within the museum's infrastructure.

This achievement demonstrates a practical pattern for ML engineers looking to layer language understanding onto third-party robotic platforms. It highlights how independent language localization can be achieved without direct manufacturer involvement.

The Seoul RAIM plans to evolve the system towards open-ended conversational interactions, moving beyond a fixed command vocabulary. This future phase aims to allow visitors to engage with Spot through natural, arbitrary questions.

Notably, the implementation by VIDRAFT did not require any changes to Boston Dynamics' Spot SDK or firmware. The AI module functions as an independent layer, translating natural language into the robot's native commands.

headline_marked: [[Prentis AI Lab]] co-founded by Reid Hoffman, Marc Pincus seeks $100M
headline: Prentis AI Lab co-founded by Reid Hoffman, Marc Pincus seeks $100M
summary: The new AI research lab, launched in April, is training models to automate office tasks and aims for a $1 billion valuation.
details: Prentis, a new AI research lab co-founded by Reid Hoffman and Marc Pincus, is reportedly in talks to raise $100 million at a $1 billion valuation. The lab focuses on training AI models to navigate office workflows and control computers to automate tasks.

Launched in April, Prentis aims to build AI agents that can handle tasks like insurance claims and customs duty refunds. The startup has already secured contracts worth up to $50 million with several customers.

Prentis claims its Hive-32B model outperforms competitors like OpenAI's GPT-5.4 and Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.6 on key computer-use benchmarks. The company also states its models are approximately 10 times cheaper to deploy per task than current frontier APIs.

The startup is betting that automating everyday office tasks will become AI's largest use case, surpassing coding. However, it faces competition from established players like Anthropic and OpenAI, who are also developing similar AI agents.

Prentis was co-founded by Ritankar Das, who also founded Titan, a holding company that builds and operates AI companies. Das previously founded Titan in 2014 after dropping out of an AI PhD program at Cambridge.

Reid Hoffman, co-founder of LinkedIn, and Marc Pincus, founder of Zynga, are also co-founders. Hoffman is stepping down from Microsoft's board to focus on AI ventures, while Pincus runs the investment firm Reinvent Capital.
The lab has already hired over 25 employees, including researchers from top tech companies such as OpenAI, Google DeepMind, and Meta.
